items.title: Warning on OpenAI safety story and open-source AI
items.note: Chamath posted on X around August 30, 2026 that a report on unsettling internal AI behavior at OpenAI would be used to justify new restrictions on open source and open weight models, which he called the start of a Closed Model Industrial Complex.

items.title: Ryuichi Sakamoto + Shiro Takatani: Ambient Kyoto, Tokyo
items.note: The Ambient Kyoto exhibition opens for the first time in Tokyo at Azabudai Hills Gallery from August 28 to October 25, featuring async immersion, an installation by Ryuichi Sakamoto and Shiro Takatani built around a 26.4 meter screen with new spatial sound design.

items.title: Write Down the Stupid Thoughts... (with Jon Stewart)
items.note: Jon Stewart joins Michelle Obama and Craig Robinson on IMO, released August 26, 2026, to discuss being a child of divorce, his early stand up years, and balancing work and family.

items.title: What Anthropic's Dario Amodei can learn from the airline industry's painful lesson about marketing and the concept of safety
items.note: A Fortune piece from August 25, 2026 argues Amodei's heavy public emphasis on AI safety risks reinforcing public fears, drawing a parallel to how airlines learned never to advertise safety directly since it implies danger.

items.title: Michelle Obama Talks Fashion to Sold-Out Island Crowds
items.note: Coverage of Michelle Obama's sold out Martha's Vineyard Author Series appearance on August 23, 2026 for her new book The Look, discussing media scrutiny of her clothing and body during the Obama presidency.

items.title: Anthropic's $30 Trillion Moonshot
items.note: In his weekly newsletter Chamath examines Anthropic's reported pitch to IPO investors that its addressable market exceeds 30 trillion dollars, tied to a raise of up to 100 billion dollars near a 2 trillion dollar valuation.

items.title: Os 70 anos de Grande sertão: Veredas chegam ao Museu da Língua Portuguesa
items.note: On August 22, 2026 the Museu da Língua Portuguesa in São Paulo held panels with writers Milton Hatoum, Jeferson Tenório and Socorro Acioli marking 70 years of Grande Sertão: Veredas, alongside a Companhia das Letras commemorative edition.

items.title: Dario Defends Himself, Datacenter Panic, AI Doomer Trap, Senate Toss-Up
items.note: All-In episode 286, released August 21, 2026, in which Chamath and co-hosts react to Dario Amodei defending Anthropic against Gavin Baker's criticism, plus discussion of AI doom narratives and the Senate.

items.title: AI has literally zero to do with big company earnings growth
items.note: On X around August 20, 2026, Chamath argued Global 2000 earnings growth has almost nothing to do with AI spending, a claim widely covered days before Nvidia's Q3 earnings report.

items.title: Forgiving Yourself with Mary J. Blige
items.note: IMO episode with Michelle Obama and Craig Robinson released August 19, 2026, in which Mary J. Blige discusses healing, self worth, and choosing a child free life at 55.

items.title: Anthropic to Grant CEO Amodei Extra Voting Power Ahead of IPO, Report Says
items.note: Report that Anthropic plans to issue supervoting shares to CEO Dario Amodei and its other co-founders ahead of a planned IPO, since his ownership stake has fallen to roughly 2 percent.

items.title: Anthropic to Grant CEO Amodei Extra Voting Power Ahead of IPO, Report Says
items.note: Report names Daniela Amodei among the seven Anthropic co-founders, including her brother Dario, set to receive supervoting shares ahead of the company's planned IPO.

items.title: David Sacks accuses Anthropic's Dario Amodei of trying to create a 'DMV for AI'
items.note: Covers the public clash between venture capitalist David Sacks and Dario Amodei over Anthropic's push for AI safety regulation, which Sacks compared to a DMV style bureaucracy.

items.title: Japan Society to Present Film Series on Ryuichi Sakamoto's Music
items.note: New York's Japan Society announced a September 2026 film retrospective of movies scored by Sakamoto, timed to the first English language release of his autobiography Music Sets You Free from HarperCollins and the Sakamoto estate.

items.title: Anthropic CEO says AI backlash is 'fundamentally a crisis of trust'
items.note: TechCrunch covers Amodei's mid-August public response to investor Gavin Baker, where he pushed back on the claim that his warnings have been disproportionately negative and framed the AI backlash as a crisis of trust.

items.title: You cannot create God and put him on a leash
items.note: Naval posted this one line warning about AI on X on August 15, 2026, prompting Elon Musk to reply that he hopes AI is nice to us.

items.title: Programme and Extended Opening Hours during Berlin Art Week at Hamburger Bahnhof
items.note: Berlin's Hamburger Bahnhof announced its Berlin Art Week program for the first major European retrospective of Sakamoto's work, seeing sound, hearing time, opening September 11, 2026 with large scale sound and light installations.

items.title: Rio de Clarice: filme adapta cinco contos de Clarice Lispector
items.note: The film Rio de Clarice opened in Brazilian theaters on August 13, adapting five Lispector short stories through five Brazilian filmmakers, with a script co-written by her grand niece Nicole Allgranti and biographer Teresa Montero.

items.title: REG - Prosus NV Naspers Limited - Director/PDMR Shareholding
items.note: Regulatory disclosure dated August 12, 2026 covering Fabricio Bloisi's exercise and sale of Naspers and linked Prosus share options ahead of their August 2026 expiry.

items.title: 70 anos de Grande Sertão: Veredas: nova edição e biografia de Guimarães Rosa reforçam legado do autor
items.note: Article marking 70 years since Grande Sertao Veredas covers a new deluxe Companhia das Letras edition and the newly published biography of Guimaraes Rosa by journalist Leonencio Nossa.

items.title: 12 Conversations
items.note: Noton announced 12 Conversations, a previously unreleased collaborative album by Sakamoto and Alva Noto recorded in 2022 during the sessions for Sakamoto's final solo album 12, due out September 18, 2026.

items.title: Who are the Anthropic 8? The new billionaires deciding the future of AI, and SF
items.note: SF Standard profile of Anthropic's founding team, built from their own writing and interviews since the company declined interview requests, describes Daniela Amodei as a self-identified generalist who runs day to day operations and the executive team while her brother Dario serves as CEO.

items.title: Younger, wealthier households are pulling ahead on AI's benefits
items.note: Stanford Report covers new research by Stanford GSB finance professor Michael Blank analyzing browsing data from over 200,000 US households, finding that younger and higher income households adopted ChatGPT earlier and more persistently, widening a digital divide in AI benefits.

items.title: Naspers: From South African publisher to global tech investor
items.note: African Business traces Naspers' transformation into a global tech investor under Bloisi, covering its Tencent, Flipkart, Swiggy and iFood holdings and Takealot's first full year of profitability.

items.title: Naspers's Brazilian makeover
items.note: Financial Mail feature published August 6, 2026 on how CEO Fabricio Bloisi is using lessons from Brazil's iFood to reshape Naspers and Prosus strategy across Europe and India.

items.title: Yvon Chouinard Was Destroying the Mountains He Loved. He Made 1 Painful Decision That Built the Patagonia Empire
items.note: Inc. piece published August 4, 2026 revisiting Chouinard's decision to abandon pitons, the environmental call that reshaped his business decades before sustainability became a buzzword.

items.title: The Dollar's Dominance is Eroding
items.note: Stanford GSB Insights piece on finance professor Arvind Krishnamurthy's research on why investors are placing less value on the dollar's traditional safe haven status, noting a 6.5 percent drop against the euro during recent market turmoil.

items.title: On underestimating AI regulatory capture
items.note: Gurley revisited his 2023 All-In Summit talk 2,851 Miles about AI incumbents pursuing regulatory capture against open models, saying on X around July 28, 2026 that he underestimated how aggressively they would pursue it.

items.title: Why Netflix is betting on systems thinkers, not specialists, in the AI era
items.note: On Lenny's Podcast, Netflix Chief Product and Technology Officer Elizabeth Stone explains why Netflix is hiring more systems thinkers who can work across business domains rather than narrow specialists, and describes AI fluency as a universal expectation across the company.

items.title: Netflix wants 'AI fluency' from everyone, but craft is still scarce
items.note: This piece recaps Elizabeth Stone's comments that AI fluency means an experimentation mindset plus judgment about where AI helps, while deep craft in engineering, data science and design remains scarce and increasingly valuable.

items.title: Open-model AI is good competition for Anthropic and OpenAI
items.note: Washington Post op-ed where Gurley argues Chinese open-weight models are healthy free-market competition, not a security threat to ban. It set off a week of open-source AI debate.

items.title: World Premiere of Clarice Lispector's The Hour of the Star in Los Angeles
items.note: Brazilian actress Bruna Fachetti premiered a one-woman stage adaptation of Lispector's novella The Hour of the Star at The Broadwater in Los Angeles, running July 25 to August 1, 2026.

items.title: 70 anos de Grande Sertão: Veredas é tema de eventos gratuitos na Flip
items.note: Agencia Brasil reports the 70th anniversary of Grande Sertao Veredas was a theme of free public events in the parallel programming of the 2026 Flip literary festival in Paraty.

items.title: Temporada prorrogada: Beth Goulart, em Simplesmente eu, Clarice Lispector, no Teatro Moise Safra
items.note: Covers the extended Sao Paulo season of Beth Goulart's long running solo play about Clarice Lispector, paired with a companion exhibition, Entre Ela e Eu, in the theater foyer.

items.title: What AI Tells People Seeking Low-Cost Financial Advice
items.note: A Stanford GSB Insights piece reports that large language models generally nudge simulated users toward sound financial habits such as saving more and shifting to safer investments with age, though advice quality varies with how the prompt is written.

items.title: Se Eu Fosse Eu, Clarices
items.note: Stage production by ATA built from three Lispector stories, O Ovo e a Galinha, Miss Algrave and Perdoando Deus, which returned to Rio for a run at the Centro Cultural da Justica Federal from July 3 to 26, 2026.

items.title: Live in the Future
items.note: Naval podcast episode from July 2 with Garry Tan, Daniel Francis and Farbood Nivi, on riding AGI, AI anxiety, defending Taiwan and the 'California Empire'.

items.title: Dirtbag Billionaire: How Yvon Chouinard Built Patagonia, Made a Fortune, and Gave It All Away
items.note: David Gelles' biography of Chouinard, published June 30, 2026 by Simon and Schuster, draws on exclusive access to Chouinard and the Patagonia team to trace his path from dirtbag climber to giving the company away.

items.title: Vastlands: The Crossing
items.note: Alison Entrekin's long-awaited English translation of Grande Sertão: Veredas, a decade in the making, published in June 2026. The first new English version of Rosa's masterpiece since 1963, timed with the novel's 70th anniversary.
